This week, the House passed several major bills to deliver help for Kansas veterans and their families. In addition to supporting the freestanding Major Richard Star Act, I supported the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, a bipartisan package that combines more than 60 veterans' bills (including a modified version of the Major Richard Star Act). Highlights include:

✅ The Veterans ACCESS Act (I am a cosponsor) – Ensures veterans can access healthcare they have earned, inside or outside the VA and without wait times.

✅ The Love Lives On Act (I am a cosponsor) – Allows surviving spouses of fallen service members and veterans to retain the VA survivor benefits their spouse earned in service, even if they remarry.

✅ The Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act – Increases monthly VA benefits for severely disabled veterans and their families, as well as veterans' survivors and Gold Star families.

We also passed the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act so veterans' benefits keep pace with the cost of living.

Veterans sacrificed to defend our freedom. I'm hopeful the Senate can find a path to get all or at least most of these measures to the President's desk so they can become law.

Last year, I cosponsored the Major Richard Star Act after Kansans brought to my attention the unfair "wounded warrior tax" that can prevent combat-wounded veterans from receiving full military retirement pay and the full disability compensation--both of which they have earned.

Good news for Kansas agriculture! 

USDA is investing nearly $4 million in Kansas meat processors to expand capacities and strengthen local processing opportunities for Kansas ranchers.

I’m especially pleased to see three of these investments in our Second Congressional District:

-Diamond A Processing (Junction City): $182,094
-Mitchell Bolling (Moran): $197,338
-Plainview Beef Company (Peabody): $2 million

These investments will support local businesses and improve opportunities for Kansas cattle producers.

Last night, the House of Representatives voted to refer proposed Articles of Impeachment against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee. In my view, that was the right thing to do.

Accusations and concerns involving Secretary Hegseth’s conduct in office

Today, we honor the men and women who have served our nation. Their courage, sacrifice, and dedication deserve our gratitude every day.

Kansas has a special place in this holiday’s history. Emporia proudly holds the distinction of being the founding city of Veterans Day, a tradition that began in 1953 to honor all who served.

I was proud to recognize Emporia’s place in our nation’s history on the House floor.

To all our veterans and their families, thank you for your service and sacrifice.

Happy Veterans Day!

Good news for rural Kansas!

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services is investing nearly $225.9 million MORE through the Rural Health Transformation Program for the coming year.

That’s an increase of $4 million above last year’s award for a two-year total of nearly $450 million--among the most for any state.

I was proud to vote for and support the legislation that established this program to deliver critical resources for rural healthcare providers and communities across Kansas.

Ensuring Kansans have access to quality healthcare, no matter where they live, remains an important priority. I’ll continue working to support rural communities across our state and especially in our 2nd Congressional District.

One of the joys of serving in Congress is the opportunity to nominate young Kansans to attend one of the U.S. service academies. Today we met with applicants at the Kansas Statehouse in Topeka. I always come away reassured that America's future will be in good hands. Thank you to all the students who are applying and to the families who support them.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
